- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates or lags; increase early forecast values by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >3%), model frequently overcorrects in next 3–5 days; apply a 1–2% downward adjustment to subsequent forecast days.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from 0.9 to 0.2), model often fails to adjust quickly; delay or reduce forecast peak by 3–5% in next 5–7 days.
- Model tends to overpredict mid-term (15–30d) if sentiment is flat or mildly positive; apply a 1–3% mean-reversion correction toward recent 7-day average.
- If sentiment is rising (increasing over last 5 days), model often underreacts; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days to capture momentum.
